ceiling: Configuration validation only, so it confirms a failure predicate, preserved constraints and the drop-failure flag are declared; it does not shrink inputs.
offer: Reduce a failing input while preserving both the failure and the relevant domain constraints. A smaller case that no longer triggers the defect is not a useful shrink result.

minimal.reason: Declare the predicate that identifies the failure. A shrinker without it cannot tell failure from success, so write the check.

mid.reason: List the domain constraints a shrunk input must keep. Violating them yields invalid cases, so name each constraint.

maximal.reason: Set dropping the failure during shrink to false. A smaller input that no longer fails is useless, so keep the failure while reducing.

rule.reason: Declare the predicate that identifies the failure. A shrinker without it cannot tell failure from success, so write the check.
